# gatecheck

> Gatecheck compares a scanner report to thresholds in a config file and exits non-zero when a limit is crossed. One binary. Stateless.

Report type comes from the file contents. The filename is the fallback when the contents are ambiguous. Coverage thresholds are ratios: 0.8 is 80 percent. Pass the config with `gatecheck validate --config`. Print the agent guide with `gatecheck agent-guide`.

## Docs

- [Installation](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/installation.html): install a release binary or build from source
- [Usage](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/usage.html): commands, logs, and exit status
- [Bootstrap](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/bootstrap.html): install Grype, Syft, Gitleaks, and osemgrep, then run them
- [CLI reference](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/cli-reference.html): flags, subcommands, and environment variables
- [Supported reports](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/supported-reports.html): how file contents and filenames select the report type
- [Configuration](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/configuration.html): config keys and threshold units
- [Validation](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/validation.html): rule order and exit codes
- [List reports](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/list-reports.html): tables, standard input, and EPSS columns
- [Bundles](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/gatecheck-bundle.html): create, add, and remove
- [Examples](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/examples.html): config, bundle, audit, and standard input
- [Library](https://docs.gatecheck.dev/library-usage.html): Go package next to the CLI
